main.title: The Banner Saga
main.subtitle: Tactical battles and the fate of a caravan
main.summary: The Banner Saga is a tactical role-playing video game developed by Stoic and published by Versus Evil. It was released for personal computers and mobile phones in 2014, for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in 2016 and for Nintendo Switch in 2018.

cards.heading: A caravan crosses a world inspired by Norse mythology
cards.text:
The Banner Saga is a tactical role-playing video game developed by Stoic and published by Versus Evil. It was released for personal computers and mobile phones in 2014, for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in 2016 and for Nintendo Switch in 2018.

Taking place in a fictional world inspired by Norse mythology, the game tells the story of the player's caravan as a whole, as they combat a warlike race named Dredge that despises humans. The game follows two playable characters whose separate stories eventually merge. The interactive story changes depending on players' decisions.

cards.heading: Tactical combat and lasting consequences
cards.text: The player builds a party with complementary abilities for a campaign of turn-based battles, influenced by Final Fantasy Tactics and Shining Force. Outside combat, decisions shape what happens to the caravan and to the two groups whose stories eventually meet. Stoic wanted players to carry defeats forward and deal with their consequences. Following a travelling community gives those choices a wider setting: the campaign continues with the people and circumstances that remain after each encounter.

cards.heading: Hand-drawn art and a crowdfunded studio
cards.text: The game's developer, Stoic Studio, was founded by three former BioWare designers. It was funded via Kickstarter, a crowdfunding platform. The hand-drawn animation and art-style featured in the game was inspired by the art of Eyvind Earle, Ralph Bakshi and Don Bluth. Austin Wintory composed the game's music, with Dallas Wind Symphony performing. The game's multiplayer component, The Banner Saga: Factions, was released as a free standalone game before the game's release.

main.title: Octodad: Dadliest Catch
main.subtitle: Everyday chores become an octopus’s challenge
main.summary: Octodad: Dadliest Catch is an independent adventure video game developed and published by Young Horses. It is a sequel to the 2010 freeware game Octodad. The game consists of controlling the protagonist Octodad in completing chores typical of the mundane suburban father, but complicated by the fact that he is an octopus in disguise.

cards.heading: An octopus tries to pass as an ordinary father
cards.text: Octodad: Dadliest Catch is an independent adventure video game developed and published by Young Horses. It is a sequel to the 2010 freeware game Octodad. The game consists of controlling the protagonist Octodad in completing chores typical of the mundane suburban father, but complicated by the fact that he is an octopus in disguise.

cards.heading: Awkward limbs and a shared cooperative challenge
cards.text: Octodad must complete ordinary family tasks while concealing that he is an octopus in human clothes. The player switches between tentacles acting as arms and legs, separately managing a step or the grasp of an object. Picking up groceries becomes difficult when reaching for one item knocks another away. Causing too much visible chaos raises suspicion and can send the player back to a checkpoint. The objectives remain familiar while the body resists performing them neatly. Cooperative play extends that problem to several people, with up to four players each trying to control one limb.

cards.heading: Family life under a fragile disguise
cards.text: Set after the events of the original game, Dadliest Catch features Octodad working around the house, going grocery shopping, and accompanying his family on a visit to the local aquarium at his wife Scarlet's request, much to his chagrin. As before, he must spend time with his wife and children while not arousing the suspicion of other humans, including the evil Chef Fujimoto, who knows Octodad's secret and seeks to expose and cook him.

main.title: TxK
main.subtitle: Watch the shape ahead of the next enemy
main.summary: TxK is Llamasoft's PlayStation Vita arcade shooter, first released in North America on 11 February 2014. Designed by Jeff Minter, it places the player at the edge of geometric playfields while enemies travel along their lanes towards the rim. Movement around that boundary and fire directed into the approaching formations create a clear central task. The changing shapes and visual effects give the action a more intense character, but success begins with reading the lanes. A threat has to be recognised early enough to reach the correct position before it arrives.

cards.heading: Watch the shape ahead of the next enemy
cards.text: TxK is Llamasoft's PlayStation Vita arcade shooter, first released in North America on 11 February 2014. Designed by Jeff Minter, it places the player at the edge of geometric playfields while enemies travel along their lanes towards the rim. Movement around that boundary and fire directed into the approaching formations create a clear central task. The changing shapes and visual effects give the action a more intense character, but success begins with reading the lanes. A threat has to be recognised early enough to reach the correct position before it arrives.

cards.heading: A power-up changes what the ship can risk
cards.text: Additional abilities expand the player's responses as a run continues, allowing the game to develop beyond the initial movement and firing pattern. An option removes those power-ups for a different kind of challenge. The player balances attention to the immediate lane with awareness of enemies elsewhere on the shape, deciding when to remain in place and when to move around the rim. The restricted path makes those decisions readable. Even when the display becomes busy, the next useful action depends on understanding which section of the boundary is about to become dangerous.

cards.heading: A Llamasoft game with a complicated afterlife
cards.text: TxK received strong reviews, with its compact arcade design finding a natural home on the Vita. Planned releases for other platforms did not proceed after Atari raised legal objections over similarities to Tempest 2000. That history left the original handheld release unusually isolated despite its favourable reception. The game belongs to Minter's long interest in combining precise shooting with intense audiovisual patterns. Its appeal comes from keeping those layers connected: the spectacle surrounds a task the player can understand immediately, then continues testing how accurately that understanding can be maintained as the shapes and threats change.

main.title: Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze
main.subtitle: Four Kongs explore the islands reclaimed by the Snowmads
main.summary: Donkey Kong and his partners cross islands reclaimed by the Snowmads, combining precise platforming with distinct companion abilities.

cards.heading: The Wii U sequel to Donkey Kong Country Returns
cards.text: Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze is a 2014 platform game developed by Retro Studios and published by Nintendo for the Wii U. The fifth installment in the Donkey Kong Country series, Tropical Freeze is a direct sequel to the 2010 Wii game Donkey Kong Country Returns and was released in February 2014. An enhanced port for the Nintendo Switch was released in May 2018.

cards.heading: Four Kongs bring different platforming abilities
cards.text: Donkey Kong crosses the islands with companions whose abilities change how the player approaches a gap or obstacle. Diddy's barrel jet pack extends a crossing, Dixie's spinning ponytail supplies an initial lift followed by a slower descent, and Cranky's cane lets him bounce over hazards such as thorns. A second player can control the companion directly. Donkey Kong can also pluck objects from the ground and throw stunned enemies. Filling the Kong-POW meter allows the pair to turn enemies on screen into useful items, with the result depending on the partner.

cards.heading: Funky Kong’s shop and challenges beyond the main route
cards.text: Funky Kong's expanded shop sells support items, including temporary invincibility, that can help with a difficult course. Kong letters and puzzle pieces encourage players to examine routes beyond the direct path; reaching some requires the right companion. These discoveries unlock bonuses and hidden levels. Time Attack gives completed courses another purpose, with online leaderboards and replays showing how highly ranked players negotiate them.

cards.heading: New perspectives and the development of Tropical Freeze
cards.text: Retro Studios began Tropical Freeze with ideas it still wanted to explore after Returns, including underwater stages and more dynamic camera work. The camera can swing away from the usual side view into a three-dimensional perspective, changing how an approaching obstacle appears. Dixie adds another way to reach platforms, while plucking objects introduces a further interaction with the scenery. Producer Michael Kelbaugh had worked on the series since its first release. Shigeru Miyamoto supplied advice on the ground pound and other details while Retro led development.

main.title: Strider
main.subtitle: Hiryu explores Kazakh City with an evolving plasma blade
main.summary: Strider, known in Japan as Strider Hiryū, is a 2014 hack and slash game developed by Double Helix Games and Capcom's Osaka studio. It was released in February 2014 for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox 360, and Xbox One. It is a reboot of the 1989 video game Strider.

cards.heading: A new interpretation of the 1989 action game
cards.text: Strider, known in Japan as Strider Hiryū, is a 2014 hack and slash game developed by Double Helix Games and Capcom's Osaka studio. It was released in February 2014 for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox 360, and Xbox One. It is a reboot of the 1989 video game Strider.

cards.heading: Exploring Kazakh with the transforming Cypher
cards.text: The player controls the series' main character, Strider Hiryu. The environment is freely explorable in search for weapons and items. Strider Hiryu's main weapon is his Cypher, a plasma weapon that can take several properties. Upgrades for the Cypher can be obtained by exploring Kazakh.

cards.heading: Combining the series’ history with a less linear world
cards.text: Double Helix worked with Capcom's Osaka studio, which supplied character and game design, to bring together elements from Hiryu's arcade, console, manga and fighting-game appearances. The team wanted a larger, less linear adventure, with exploration rewarding the player with further abilities. Giving the Cypher different properties connected the weapon's development to that progression. Hiryu's recurring struggle with Grandmaster Meio supplied the story, while surveys and fan discussions had helped demonstrate continued interest in the series.

main.title: Castlevania: Lords of Shadow 2
main.subtitle: Dracula regains his powers in an open-world conclusion
main.summary: MercurySteam's action adventure follows a weakened Dracula as he recovers his powers across medieval and modern settings.

cards.heading: Dracula’s story crosses medieval and modern worlds
cards.text: Castlevania: Lords of Shadow 2 is MercurySteam's 2014 action adventure for Konami, continuing the story begun in Lords of Shadow. Gabriel Belmont has become Dracula, weakened and drawn into a conflict with Satan across medieval and modern settings. Recovering his powers gives the campaign its progression, while a more open world lets the player choose routes through the connected locations. Combat remains central, with different weapons giving Dracula ways to regain health or break an enemy's defence.

cards.heading: The Shadow Whip, Void Sword and Chaos Claws
cards.text: Dracula's Shadow Whip provides his main attacks, while the Void Sword and Chaos Claws give the player different priorities in a fight. The sword restores health when it hits; the claws break through defences and deliver heavy blows. Selecting between them therefore changes what an attack achieves as well as its appearance. Drinking an enemy's blood supplies another way to recover health. The opening briefly shows Dracula at full strength before the campaign makes rebuilding those abilities part of the journey.

cards.heading: An explorable world and a freely controlled camera
cards.text: Exploration also depends on Dracula's changing forms. A rat can hide or move through vents, mist can pass through bars and reach higher platforms, and briefly possessing an enemy can open a secure doorway. The freely controlled camera helps the player examine these routes. MercurySteam redesigned its engine and moved towards connected spaces to give the sequel more room for exploration. The medieval and modern settings place the same supernatural abilities in different kinds of surroundings.

main.title: Plants vs. Zombies: Garden Warfare
main.subtitle: Plants and zombies meet in cooperative and competitive battles
main.summary: Plants vs. Zombies: Garden Warfare (commonly abbreviated as PVZGW or GW1) is a 2014 third-person shooter video game developed by PopCap Vancouver and published by Electronic Arts. The third game in the Plants vs. Zombies franchise, it revolves around plants defending humankind from a zombie invasion. In the game, players assume control of either the Plants (under Crazy Dave) or the Zombies (under Dr. Zomboss), as they fight in various cooperative and competitive multiplayer modes. Upon completing matches and finishing objectives, players earn coins to acquire stickers that unlock customization items and character variants.

cards.heading: Plants and zombies enter a team-based shooter
cards.text: Plants vs. Zombies: Garden Warfare (commonly abbreviated as PVZGW or GW1) is a 2014 third-person shooter video game developed by PopCap Vancouver and published by Electronic Arts. The third game in the Plants vs. Zombies franchise, it revolves around plants defending humankind from a zombie invasion. In the game, players assume control of either the Plants (under Crazy Dave) or the Zombies (under Dr. Zomboss), as they fight in various cooperative and competitive multiplayer modes. Upon completing matches and finishing objectives, players earn coins to acquire stickers that unlock customization items and character variants.

cards.heading: Eight classes with distinct combat abilities
cards.text: Each side has four classes with different jobs. A Peashooter or Foot Soldier handles general fighting, support characters help the team, and a Cactus attacks from range. Individual abilities make those roles more specific: a Peashooter throws a Chili Bean Bomb, while a Chomper burrows beneath a zombie before attacking. Flower Pots and Bone Piles let players add computer-controlled units to the field. The match combines the actions of the team with the smaller forces its members choose to deploy.

cards.heading: Sticker packs, challenges and character variants
cards.text: Matches and class challenges earn coins and progress towards upgrades, accessories and character variants. Coins buy sticker packs, whose contents go into the player's collection; five stickers complete the picture needed to unlock a variant. Variants can change how a familiar class fights. Commando Pea replaces explosive shots with automatic fire, while Cricket Star adds fire damage. PopCap later introduced purchases for real money, giving players another way to obtain packs. The sticker book records what has been unlocked.

cards.heading: Garden Ops and cooperative ways to play
cards.text: Garden Ops gives up to four players a garden to defend through ten waves of zombies. Some waves introduce bosses, and surviving the last assault leads to an escape: the plants must reach an extraction point and stay alive until evacuation. Boss Mode places Crazy Dave or Dr. Zomboss above the field, using scans, healing and air strikes to support the team below. The PlayStation 4 and Xbox One editions also offer a two-player cooperative mode on a shared screen.

main.title: Thief
main.subtitle: Garrett returns to a city of shadows
main.summary: Eidos-Montréal's Thief returned Garrett to a new version of the City in 2014.

cards.heading: Garrett observes the City from a first-person perspective
cards.text: Thief is Eidos-Montréal's 2014 first-person stealth game, returning Garrett to a new version of the City. Wealth, poverty and political unrest shape the place through which the master thief moves. Watching a doorway or a passing guard helps the player decide where to go and when to cross an exposed space. Reaching a destination unnoticed depends on reading those small openings in the surroundings.

cards.heading: Routes without killing or raising the alarm
cards.text: The studio described routes through the game without killing anyone, and even without causing an enemy alert. Such goals change the value of waiting, observing and finding another way around. A successful escape can be more important than defeating the person blocking the obvious path.

cards.heading: Interface options and the risk of Iron Man mode
cards.text: The available options include removing the onscreen interface and enabling an Iron Man mode that ends a run when Garrett dies. These settings alter how much information and safety the player receives. They make the same City support different tolerances for uncertainty and failure.

main.title: South Park: The Stick of Truth
main.subtitle: The New Kid joins South Park’s fantasy war
main.summary: South Park: The Stick of Truth is a 2014 role-playing video game developed by Obsidian Entertainment in collaboration with South Park Digital Studios and published by Ubisoft.

cards.heading: The New Kid enters the battle for the Stick of Truth
cards.text: South Park: The Stick of Truth is a 2014 role-playing video game developed by Obsidian Entertainment in collaboration with South Park Digital Studios and published by Ubisoft. Based on the American animated television series South Park, the game follows the New Kid, who has moved to the eponymous town and becomes involved in an epic role-play fantasy war involving humans, wizards, and elves, who are fighting for control of the all-powerful Stick of Truth. Their game quickly escalates out of control, bringing them into conflict with aliens, Nazi zombies, and gnomes, threatening the entire town with destruction.

cards.heading: Exploring South Park and fighting with a party
cards.text: The game is played from a 2.5D, third-person perspective replicating the aesthetic of the television series. The New Kid is able to freely explore the town of South Park, interacting with characters and undertaking quests, and accessing new areas by progressing through the main story. By selecting one of four character archetypes, Fighter, Thief, Mage, or Jew, each offering specific abilities, the New Kid and a supporting party of characters use a variety of melee, ranged, and magical fart attacks to combat with their enemies.

cards.heading: Parker, Stone and Obsidian shape the adventure
cards.text: Development began in 2009 after South Park creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone approached Obsidian about making a role-playing game designed to look exactly like the television series. Parker and Stone were involved throughout the game's production: they wrote its script, consulted on the design, and as in the television program, they voiced many of the characters. South Park: The Stick of Truth's production was turbulent; following the bankruptcy of the original publisher, THQ, the rights to the game were acquired by Ubisoft in early 2013, and its release date was postponed several times from its initial date in March 2013 to its eventual release in March 2014, for PlayStation 3, Windows, and Xbox 360.

cards.heading: Censorship, critical reception and later releases
cards.text: South Park: The Stick of Truth was subject to censorship in some regions because of its content, which includes abortions and Nazi imagery; Parker and Stone replaced the scenes with detailed explanations of what occurs in each scene. The game was released to positive reviews, which praised the comedic script, visual style, and faithfulness to the source material. It received criticism for a lack of challenging combat and technical issues that slowed or impeded progress. A sequel, South Park: The Fractured but Whole, was released in October 2017, and South Park: The Stick of Truth was re-released in February 2018, for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, and on Nintendo Switch in September 2018.

main.title: Hearthstone
main.subtitle: Warcraft becomes a turn-based card game
main.summary: Hearthstone is a 2014 free-to-play digital collectible card video game produced by Blizzard Entertainment. Originally subtitled Heroes of Warcraft, Hearthstone builds upon the existing lore of the Warcraft series by using the same elements, characters, and relics. The game is available on the Windows, macOS, iOS and Android platforms, featuring cross-platform play. It has been a critical and commercial success, with Blizzard reporting more than 100 million Hearthstone players as of November 2018, and the game has become popular as an esport, with cash prize tournaments hosted by Blizzard and other organizers.

cards.heading: Warcraft characters enter a digital card game
cards.text: Hearthstone is a 2014 free-to-play digital collectible card video game produced by Blizzard Entertainment. Originally subtitled Heroes of Warcraft, Hearthstone builds upon the existing lore of the Warcraft series by using the same elements, characters, and relics. The game is available on the Windows, macOS, iOS and Android platforms, featuring cross-platform play. It has been a critical and commercial success, with Blizzard reporting more than 100 million Hearthstone players as of November 2018, and the game has become popular as an esport, with cash prize tournaments hosted by Blizzard and other organizers.

cards.heading: Decks, heroes and the pursuit of new cards
cards.text: The game is a turn-based card game between two opponents, using constructed decks of 30 cards along with a selected hero with a unique power. Players use their limited mana crystals to play abilities or summon minions to attack the opponent, with the goal of destroying the opponent's hero. Winning matches and completing quests earn in-game gold, rewards in the form of new cards, and other in-game prizes. Players can then buy packs of new cards through gold or microtransactions to customize and improve their decks. The game features several modes of play, including casual and ranked matches, drafted arena battles, and single-player adventures. New content for the game involves the addition of new card sets and gameplay, taking the form of expansion packs.

cards.heading: A small experimental team adapts physical cards
cards.text: A small Blizzard team developed Hearthstone from a shared enthusiasm for collectible card games. Existing characters, concepts and illustrations from the physical World of Warcraft Trading Card Game supplied part of its foundation. The interface aimed to preserve the feel of handling a physical card game while keeping play direct on a screen. This smaller experimental project brought Warcraft's familiar material into a different kind of contest, built around decks, heroes and successive turns.

cards.heading: Mana and turn limits keep the game moving
cards.text: Mana sets a changing budget for each turn. The allowance increases by one until it reaches ten, while cards have different costs. The player must decide which available combination is worth playing now and which cards should remain in hand for a later turn. A turn timer keeps those decisions moving. The opponent has no manual reactions to perform during that turn, allowing its sequence of plays to proceed without repeated pauses for a response.
